correctness.rationale: The stated maxima and equality classification follow analytically. A rectangle c+[-u,u]+[-v,v] in central-symmetric K can be centered by averaging with its reflected copy without changing side lengths. With p=u+v and q=u-v, p,q have equal norm and perimeter 2(|p+q|+|p-q|). This expression is separately convex on K×K, hence bounded above by vertex pairs; equal vertex radii R make each distinct diameter-pair vertex rectangle feasible, so the bound is attained. Strict convexity in each argument away from collinearity excludes nonvertex centered maximizers; a collinear pair only yields 4R and is suboptimal. For any off-center maximizer with vertex p of norm R, |c+p|²+|c-p|²≤2R² forces c=0. The angular identity gives 4√2 R cos(ε/2); nearest-perpendicular pairs are found by the monotone two-pointer scan on sorted diameter angles. For regular even n the defect is 0 or π/n, and the stated counts follow by cyclic partner enumeration. Inspected verify_rectangle.py tests n=4..602 and 104 additional samples; these finite checks are not the universal proof.
residual_risks: Requires both central symmetry and equal-radius cyclic vertices; the proof is not claimed for arbitrary convex polygons or prescribed-aspect rectangles.
The O(m) comparison bound assumes pre-sorted cyclic vertices and exact real angular comparisons; ties and finite-bit complexity are outside scope.
